'''Jūnisho Jinja''' (十二所神社), also referred to as '''Jūnisha Jinja''' (十二社神社), '''Jūni Hashira Jinja''' (十二柱神社), or '''Jūni Tenjin Jinja''' (十二天神社), are [[Shinto shrine|Shinto shrines]] found throughout [[Japan]]. Some of these shrines are also called '''Jūnishō''' (十二社). 

These shrines can be categorized into two main types:
1. Shrines dedicated to local mountain deities called '''Jūni-sama''' (Twelve Lords), associated with ancient rituals and the customs of the "Twelve Lectures." These shrines are primarily found in mountainous areas of eastern Japan, especially in the northern [[Kantō region]] and [[Kōshin'etsu region]]. Research indicates that 65% of the 438 shrines named Jūnisho or Jūnisha enshrine [[Ōyamatsumi]] as their main deity.
2. Shrines that enshrine the [[Kumano shrine|Kumano Sanzan]] deities (known as [[Kumano Gongen]]). These were originally called '''Jūnisho Gongen-sha'''. During the [[Meiji era]], many of these shrines modified their enshrined deities to the "[[Kamiyonanayo]]" and "[[Five Generations of Earth Deities]]," or the "Twelve Gods of the Heavenly Generation."
